name: Jivial Industries Limited
summary:
Jivial is a very small manufacturer of finished aluminium railings and fixtures, now attempting a much larger extrusion/backward-integration and GFRP expansion. It is not an aluminium smelter. Reported growth and legacy accounting returns are attractive, but neither establishes a durable competitive advantage or cash-generative new plant. FY26 revenue/PAT of ₹17.6343 cr/₹3.7540 cr are corroborated in a reproduced directors report; CFO was only about ₹0.5443 cr. Cumulative FY23–25 audited/restated CFO/PAT is 27.1%, falling to 13.4% after lease/security deposits. Inventory and receivables, rather than exceptional income, are the central economic concern.

At the dated 19 October ₹78.10 close, issued equity value is ₹36.4696 cr and static FY26 P/E is 9.72×. The 60% decline from the ₹196 IPO price is not a margin of safety by itself. A fully specified conditional annual base case produces 19.47% return, but that number is not eligible for R: actual October unrestricted cash, IPO deployment, exact opening claim composition and the January–October balance bridge are missing. The underlying growth basis also remains unresolved: the one full post-acquisition annual comparison lacks a complete volume/price–mix bridge and comparable interim history, so REV, BQS and GQS remain NS rather than fabricated point scores. This is a completed substantive deep review with targeted evidence holds, not a favorable investment recommendation. Classification: research hold / cash-conversion and execution watchlist; no compounder designation.

sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
Information cutoff 20 October 2026; price date 19 October 2026; nominal INR equity hurdle 15%; five annual periods ending 19 October 2027–2031; reference position ₹5 lakh, not a recommendation for the user's portfolio. Jivial Industries Limited, BSE SME544805/JIVIAL, ISIN INE0 V3 T01017, incorporated 23 June 2021 and converted to public company 1 January 2024. CIN U28999 GJ2021 PLC123516. Listing 1 July 2026; post-IPO shares 4,669,600. Accounts are standalone Indian GAAP/AS, no verified subsidiary/NCI complexity. A trading lot is 600 shares; the IPO minimum application was 1,200 shares, two lots.

G1 integrity: no substantiated severe failure established. Related-party property and predecessor acquisition warrant scrutiny, not allegations of diversion. G2 reliability: targeted hold on the current investment model and organic-growth comparability. Financial annexures are much more reliable than inconsistent promotional KPI tables; the latest signed annual notes and current cash/deployment bridge remain unavailable. This is not a finding that all historic accounts are false. G3 funding: uncertain, not failed. Low historical debt and received IPO proceeds support the business, but earmarks and an unresolved machinery quote/GST allocation matter. Restrained essential operations survive in the disclosed conditional test; a linked committed-project stress has a cash gap. A modeled stress gap is not evidence of an actual default. G4 tradability: implementation hold: 44/60 turnover rows recovered and median 5% whole-lot capacity is demonstrably zero; exact missing-day status/current restrictions remain unavailable.

High confidence: identity, original prospectus financial facts and IPO terms. Medium: FY26 reproduced P&L/audit, approximate balance sheet, historical qualitative judgments. Low: exact October cash/claims, commissioned capacity and organic acquisition-adjusted growth. Missing evidence is not scored neutral 5.

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
Canonical factors: GOV 5, MOAT 4, REV NS, DUR 5, CAP 5, CASH 2, BAL 5, EXEC 5, EARN 5, R NS, D4, P5; L remains NS after the bounded liquidity review. Each factor has a separate evidence/contrary-evidence audit. GOV 5 is mixed stewardship, not a governance clearance. CASH 2 reflects persistent realized weakness, not merely a first-year growth investment. CAP 5 does not ignore high legacy returns; it recognizes that they do not prove returns on the much larger funded project. BAL 5 assesses the identifiable low-debt structure, while G3 remains an uncertainty about dated funding, not an arbitrary failure.

BQS known contribution 3.90, coverage 88%, missing-data mathematical bound 4.02–5.10 before one-decimal display, not a confidence interval. GQS known contribution 2.70, coverage 60%, mathematical bound 3.10–6.70; the persistent CASH≤3 cap would limit any scoreable final GQS to 5.0. Do not replace NS with the cap. IAS is NS because Q/BQS, R and initially L are incomplete; no renormalization or midpoint. Scores and bounds are analyst judgments, not verified facts. BQS/GQS ranking eligibility is withheld for the specific underlying REV evidence gap, despite one comparable post-acquisition annual growth observation; IAS has separate current-funding/model and implementation gaps. Resolving liquidity alone will not make any investment ranking eligible. CAP and GOV ±1 sensitivity moves BQS known contribution±0.12 and±0.20 respectively; CAP and EARN ±1 each move GQS±0.15. A0.1-point comparison would be false precision.

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
Jivial buys unfinished aluminium extrusions/castings, then cuts, drills, anodizes, buffs/polishes and powder-coats them. Products include bottom glass-holding profiles, handrails, spigots, bends, brackets, jointers, locks and endcaps. Revenue depends on design/specification, finish, availability, channel service and material prices, not only tonnes of aluminium. Buyers include fabricators, glass suppliers, construction SMEs, architects and interior designers. Orders are purchase-order based, without long-term customer or supplier commitments. The prospectus reports 35 distributors and customer count increasing 291→327; those relationships are useful distribution, not contractual recurring revenue.

FY25 railings ₹9.3883 cr contributed 78.2%, fixtures ₹2.0122 cr 16.76%, other ₹0.6055 cr 5.04%. In 9 MDecember 25 railings reached ₹9.8849 cr 81.6%, fixtures ₹0.573 cr 4.73%, other ₹1.6557 cr 13.67%. This large mix shift must be understood before extrapolating margins. Gujarat/Maharashtra/Chhattisgarh represented 72.86% of FY25 sales and 78.97% of 9 MDecember 25 sales. The business is regionally concentrated rather than an already national franchise.

Unit I is about 6,500 sqft and leased; the larger Unit II is about 40,000 sqft, also leased. There were 19 permanent staff at 31 May 2026 and 15–18 daily workers. The first plant's small asset base, outsourced job work and related-party lease economics partly explain high legacy capital returns. The proposed extrusion presses change power, tooling, maintenance, process-control and working-capital requirements. GFRP is a new adjacent capability, not proven demand automatically created by capex.

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
MOAT 4: finish, design assortment and local distributor service are real but contestable advantages. No independently verified market share, customer retention cohort, price premium or exclusive specification was found. Suppliers and customers are not locked in by long-term contracts. The company describes three patents, but the detailed evidence includes registered industrial designs, not verified broad utility-patent protection; the trademark was promoter-owned and assigned 5 July 2024. Do not turn that wording into a proprietary-technology moat.

Top-ten suppliers supplied about 87% of FY25 purchases, and the largest about 40.7%. Customer concentration is rising, but the exact latest figure is internally inconsistent: the risk section reports ₹7.7215 cr/63.74%; detailed customer amounts total ₹7.2215 cr, which divided by ₹12.1135 cr is 59.62%, versus a printed 59.04%. The largest listed customer is about 22.2%. These are not three independent confirmations. The defensible conclusion is material concentration plus a disclosure reconciliation gap, not the most favorable percentage.

Peer economics show why a mechanical aluminium-sector P/E is inappropriate. ANB Metal Cast is an extrusion manufacturer: official FY26 standalone revenue ₹225.1908 cr, PAT ₹21.4596 cr, derived ex-other-income EBITDA ₹32.4507 cr/14.4%, and CFO−₹38.3258 cr. Its weak cash flow is a sector funding warning, not an excuse for Jivial. Euro Panel's issuer FY26 consolidated headline is about ₹503.20 cr revenue/₹26.56 cr PAT, roughly 5.3% net margin, but aluminium composite façade panels have different inputs/channel/brand economics. Sudal is a more established extrusion comparator for the proposed backward integration, not a like-for-like finished-railings valuation. Jivial's FY26 derived 27.5% EBITDA margin is much higher, making mix, normalization and competitive durability essential questions. Peer multiples were not independently established at the cutoff, so no spurious target multiple average is used.

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
Audited/restated FY23/FY24/FY25 revenue was ₹8.3993/₹11.0573/₹12.0061 cr. FY26 independently reproduced revenue is ₹17.6343 cr. Annual additions were ₹2.6580 cr,₹0.9488 cr and ₹5.6282 cr; growth 31.65%, 8.58% and 46.88% by exact table amounts (management rounds 46.98%, which does not exactly match those amounts). FY23–25 CAGR is 19.56% across two intervals, not the prospectus KPI's 12.65% calculation. Reported FY23–26 three-year CAGR is 28.05%. Five/ten-year CAGRs are unavailable: incorporation was 2021 and FY22 is a short initial period, not a six-observation five-year record.

The September 2023 acquisition of promoter Anand's predecessor business for ₹0.51 cr created ₹0.4246 cr goodwill. Acquired sales/profits and like-for-like organic revenue are not separately disclosed. Production grew: railings 100,800→140,890→156,330 running feet in FY23–25, fixtures 110,400→152,460→169,400 pieces. These corroborate activity growth but do not isolate acquisition, mix or selling prices. FY25 and FY26 are genuinely comparable full post-acquisition years, with 46.88% reported growth, so the older transaction alone is not a reason to withhold REV. Nevertheless, this supplies only one annual comparison; complete FY26 railings/fixtures/GFRP volumes, realization and a price–mix bridge are missing, while disclosed product mix changed sharply. Comparable prior interim data are also unavailable. Those gaps prevent a reliable underlying multi-year growth basis, rather than merely a long history, so REV remains NS after reassessment. A conservative score is not invented simply to complete the aggregate.

The 9 MDecember 25 figures are ₹12.1135 cr revenue and ₹2.9477 cr restated PAT. They are not annualized into a forecast, and their cash flow is not compared with a full year as a growth rate. FY26 minus 9 M gives an indicative ₹5.5208 cr final-quarter revenue, but no prior comparable 9 M/quarter series supports a trustworthy TTM or interim trajectory adjustment. As of the cutoff, FY26 is the latest complete year recovered, not a claim that all FY27 trading is known.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Legacy annual capacity is 193,000 running feet of railings and 242,000 fixtures; FY25 production implies 81%/70% utilization. Nine-month output 128,828 feet/141,570 fixtures equals 66.75%/58.5% of annual capacity, not evidence of a full-year utilization collapse. Planned capacity 1.58 million feet/1.985 million fixtures is about 8.2× current nameplate. GFRP capacity 420 MT with 61.74 MT9 M production is far from mature utilization; proposed capacity is 1,248 MT. Capacity is an upper production constraint, not a forecast of orders or sales.

Fresh IPO proceeds ₹26.64816 cr less stated ₹4.2543 cr expenses produce ₹22.39386 cr net: ₹14.4 cr machinery,₹4.0 cr renovation and ₹3.99386 cr general corporate purposes. The ₹5.33904 cr OFS belongs to selling promoters, not the company. Substantial lead-manager/underwriting/selling expenses are disclosed, but fee size alone does not prove misconduct. The signed allotment advertisement shows 103,200 shares devolved on underwriters,6.32% of the offered issue, after an individual-category shortfall; this tempers claims of enthusiastic validated demand.

The machinery table totals ₹14.251209 cr excluding GST, while the ₹14.4 cr allocation includes 18% GST. An unchanged quoted scope would need ₹16.81643 cr machinery cash, plus ₹4.006303 cr renovation: ₹20.82273 cr versus ₹18.4 cr earmarked, a ₹2.42273 cr gross-cash difference before extra freight/installation. The issuer explicitly permits revising machinery/model/quantity, and says shortfalls may use internal accruals, GCP or debt. No definitive machine orders existed at 17 June; quotations dated 8–9 June generally last 180 days/six months, electrical quote five months. All quoted equipment may not ultimately be bought unchanged. This is an unresolved scope/timing budget inconsistency, not proof of a certain overrun or default.

The model separates gross GST cash from possible input-tax-credit realization. Base assumes no cash recovery and depreciates a net-of-GST illustrative basis, not double-expensing GST. Conditional half/full machinery-GST recovery in year 2 is shown separately; eligibility, output-tax offset and timing are unverified, and no instant refund is assumed. Capex needs order/advance, delivery, installation, qualification and commercial-ramp evidence. September management says no deviation from objects, but no signed deployment reconciliation was recovered. Promises-versus-delivery: current capacity/production is verified through December; IPO completed June/July; machine procurement, commissioning and productive sales remain ND at 20 October. The base ends ₹42.74 cr sales,2.42× FY26, below nameplate's 8× expansion but still requires customers and working-capital discipline, not merely capacity.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Promoters are Anand Jitendrabhai Chovatiya and Sheetalben Anand Chovatiya; management biographies claim roughly 9/6 years relevant experience. Post-IPO promoter-group ownership is about 61.17%, including the father, not just the two selling promoters'58.58%. A majority stake provides alignment and control; it does not establish minority protection. There is no verified pledge percentage as of the cutoff, so zero pledge is not assumed.

Governance areas to watch: the promoter's business acquisition, predecessor goodwill, promoter-origin trademark and Unit II property owned by related parties. Unit II's ten-year lease began 1 January 2025; substantial public-funded renovation on leased related-party property needs enforceable tenure, renewal and improvement-recovery protections. Prospectus security deposits reached ₹0.8971 cr; a ₹0.435 cr related-party deposit was disclosed in FY24. Management states transactions are in the ordinary course/arm's length and the vendors for new machinery are unrelated. Those responses are recorded, not accepted as independent proof or ignored. Past promoter remuneration was ₹0.27 cr FY25, whereas 9 MDecember pay disclosures differ; sustainable compensation must not be assumed permanently zero.

SVJK/Ankit Singhal's 22 July 2026 audit opinion, independently reproduced, is unmodified; CARO reports no loan default, no material fraud noticed/reported, no cash losses, no statutory auditor resignation during the year, and no identified material uncertainty about meeting existing liabilities within a year. Its caveat is explicit: this is not a guarantee of future solvency. Prior auditors differ across years, but routine changes and a current no-resignation report are not evidence of fraud. An audit-trail-feature statement is not a blanket verified claim of year-round operational logging.

Prospectus discloses two company tax demands totaling ₹74,750 under adjudication, not criminal convictions: ₹37,830 dated 27 February 2025 and ₹36,920 dated 15 May 2026. A small non-promoter-director demand ₹1,038 is also disclosed. No material criminal/civil/promoter proceedings were disclosed at 17 June. The later audit says no pending litigation materially affecting financial position, but does not prove those small demands were adjudicated in the company's favor. Fire NOC was applied for/pending at the prospectus date and an LEI expiry was 7 July 2026; subsequent renewal/approval remains ND, not a confirmed post-expiry violation. KPI and customer-total inconsistencies reduce disclosure confidence; they are not allegations of manipulation.

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
The accompanying comparable history retains reported versus reconstructed figures and source confidence. FY23/24/25/26 ex-other-income EBITDA, computed as PBT+finance+depreciation−other income, is ₹1.4247/₹3.0797/₹3.7495/₹4.8489 cr; margins 16.96%/27.85%/31.23%/27.50%. Small bank charges included in finance make this a standard reconciliation rather than a perfectly normalized cost measure. FY26 standardized vendors show roughly ₹5.03 cr operating profit; an investment-loss classification around ₹0.182 cr may explain the difference, but original notes are unavailable, so that add-back is not adopted as a proven recurring gain. Earlier other income includes packing/forwarding income, economically operating: stripping all of it is a conservative standardized bridge, not a definitive nonrecurring label.

PAT is ₹1.1669/₹2.4130/₹2.9715 cr restated, then ₹3.7540 cr FY26 statutory reproduction. FY25 statutory ₹2.9628 cr versus restated ₹2.9715 cr differs by ₹0.0087 cr tax adjustment; do not manufacture growth by mixing them. FY24 analogous adjustment and small rounding discrepancies are retained. FY26 statutory EPS ₹11.34 uses 3.31 million historical weighted shares; on 4.6696 million currently issued shares the same PAT is ₹8.04, not ₹11.34. The fresh issue expanded share count 41.08%; future profits must earn on that larger capital. There were no verified dividends; no warrant/ESOP dilution is assumed without allotment evidence.

CFO ₹0.1678/₹0.6301/₹0.9800 cr totaled ₹1.7779 cr versus ₹6.5514 cr PAT,27.14% conversion. Deduct ₹0.8971 cr deposits classified investing in the prospectus and conversion is 13.44%. Some standardized histories show FY24 CFO−₹0.2399 cr instead of ₹0.6301 cr: the ₹0.87 cr difference is precisely the deposit reclassification, not missing cash. FY25 analogous ₹0.0271 cr explains ₹0.9529 cr versus ₹0.98 cr. FY23–25 CFO minus cash capex/acquisition and deposits sums about−₹1.1612 cr. Financing and retained accrual profits, not owner-distributable cash, funded the balance-sheet expansion. With provisional FY26 CFO ₹0.5443 cr, FY24–26 reported conversion is 23.57%; its FY26 capex is approximately ₹1.698 cr, leaving negative cash after investment.

Inventory rose ₹0.8737→₹2.4068→₹4.6873→₹7.2230 cr at FY23/24/25/December 25, then about ₹6.64 cr FY26. Receivables were ₹0.7953/₹1.0717/₹1.0490/₹1.0170 cr, then roughly ₹3.71 cr FY26. The March spike matters more than the apparently reassuring December balance. Closing receivables/sales rises about 31.9 days FY25 to 76.8 days FY26; these are closing-balance proxies, not average collection days. Inventory days must use cost/purchase economics rather than divide by revenue and call it operational turnover. December receivables older than one year total ₹0.0802 cr with no doubtful provision; the latest ageing is unavailable. FY26 core inventory+AR−trade payables is ₹8.92 cr,50.6% of sales before other operating advances. Low bank leverage cannot make this funding intensity disappear.

Capital efficiency is reconstructed rather than quoted mechanically. Operating IC includes inventory, receivables, operating advances/prepaids less trade/customer/statutory/salary/expense liabilities, plus PPE, goodwill, CWIP, deposits and capital advances. It excludes cash, NFO investment, preliminary/miscellaneous deferred expenses, deferred tax and net tax balances. IC is ₹1.6068/₹5.3127/₹7.8430 cr FY23–25; the equity+debt bridge matches within ₹0.0001 cr. At the prospectus normal 17.16% tax rate, average-IC ROIC is 70.9% FY24 and 44.7% FY25; FY23–25 incremental proxy 28.35%. These impressive legacy ratios benefit from low initial assets, mix/margin improvement and acquisition, and do not isolate return on new capital. December IC already ₹12.2656 cr; don't annualize 9 M NOPAT. Future ₹20 cr gross project spending is a fundamentally larger cohort. No exact FY26 ROIC is claimed without notes. Ordinary lease rent stays within operating margins; no fictional lease debt is added to an unadjusted EBITDA multiple.

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
Model files provide every annual revenue, EBITDA, depreciation, tax, ONWC change, capex, opening claim payment, debt repayment and cash rollforward. This is an explicit five-year equity cash/terminal-value model, not P/E plus an unfinanced TAM. Price ₹78.10×4,669,600=₹36.469576 cr market value; FY26 static P/E9.72×. Pro-forma March equity plus net IPO is roughly ₹34.86 cr/₹74.66 per share before subsequent activity, but inventory, debtor quality, deferred expenses and leased-site assets mean book value is not a liquidation floor. Current EV is not asserted by subtracting all received IPO cash as if unrestricted and undeployed.

Synthetic opening uses March 26 rounded cash ₹0.21 cr plus IPO GCP ₹3.99386 cr as free cash,₹18.4 cr restricted, debt ₹0.98 cr, core ONWC ₹8.92 cr and ₹1.32 cr other current claims. This is not an observed October balance: intervening CFO, spending, fees, receivable changes and project commitments require a stub bridge. The model assumes zero unverified stub net cash gain and shows−₹2 cr/−₹4 cr uses. Every opening claim is mapped: ₹1.43 cr trade payables is already inside core ONWC and not paid twice; ₹1.32 cr excluded tax/statutory/employee/customer/expense/other liabilities is paid once in year 1; debt is paid once, about ₹0.245 cr annually for four years, consistent only approximately with documented bank loans maturing 2030. Paying all debt immediately is a sensitivity, not an invented distress schedule. Unclassified ₹2.44 cr other assets are not added to free cash or terminal recovery, so no assumed tax refund, deposit release or NFO realization offsets claims. Capital/acquisition payable composition is unresolved: any such amount must be reclassified from trade/other buckets, not added twice, before a current valuation is eligible. Completed acquisition consideration was cash spending in FY24; no additional outstanding seller claim was identified, but latest note confirmation is still required.

IPO expenses are deducted once in the fresh-proceeds bridge. Prior prepaid expenses could overlap: ₹0.4382 cr existed at December 25, but March/October exact fee prepayment/payable composition and OFS cost reimbursement are unknown. A ₹0.4382 cr illustrative cash-credit sensitivity is shown, not assumed as received or a verified upper bound. Other-current-claim 0–₹1.32 cr sensitivities bracket fee overlap for that bucket; they are not a complete bound on all unknown October claims. Earmarked proceeds fund only the project. Gross quoted project cash ₹20.82273 cr is charged year 1, including ₹2.42273 cr from flexible cash; no discretionary later growth capex beyond 2% maintenance is modeled because the funded project's nameplate exceeds scenario output. The base 17.16% tax follows the prospectus shelter schedule; 25.17% is a sensitivity, not legal advice. No new loans, dividends or unverified warrant proceeds enter ordinary cases. Net GST is not expensed twice; possible recovery is separate. Annual cash being positive does not prove within-year liquidity or purchase-order payment timing. Quoted renovation is modeled incremental to existing CWIP; any reimbursement or overlap must reduce remaining cash cost consistently, not be treated as additional value. Exact existing-CWIP depreciation is not reconstructed from missing FY26 notes.

Bear/base/bull revenue paths respectively end ₹18.66/₹42.74/₹65.28 cr; EBITDA margins end 18%/24%/27%, core NWC 60%/48%/44% plus 2% of incremental sales for other operating assets, terminal multiples 5×/7×/9×. These represent demand/ramp and cash-efficiency assumptions, not management guidance. Base growth 15%, 22%, 22%, 20%, 18% is already a successful commercial ramp. Conditional terminal prices ₹57.94/₹190.08/₹390.11 produce−5.80%/19.47%/37.95% annual returns. Minimum free cash ₹1.64/₹2.86/₹3.26 cr remains positive under the specified opening assumptions; no unfunded return is shown. Base year 5 EBITDA ₹10.2577 cr×7 plus ₹16.9556 cr accumulated free cash, debt zero, bridges to equity ₹88.7596 cr. The multiple applies to an earning operation, so no PPE/book value is added again. Five-year value realization depends wholly on terminal sale in this no-distribution model; terminal operating value is about 80.9% of terminal equity, the rest retained free cash.

At 12%/15%/18% hurdles, the base implied entry prices are about ₹107.86/₹94.50/₹83.09. These are conditional outputs, not target recommendations. A two-way 5%–25% constant growth/5×–9× multiple matrix is saved. With 24% EBITDA margin,50% core NWC and 7× exit, the current price requires about 14.03% annual sales growth to meet 15%, after funding capex/claims. This is achievable in physical capacity terms but not conservative evidence of demand or cash discipline. Tax 25.17% reduces base return to 18.85%; 3% maintenance to 19.05%; a−₹2 cr opening-cash stub to 18.93%, while−₹4 cr causes an early cash shortfall and suppresses ordinary return. Conditional year 2 recovery of half/full machinery GST gives 19.81%/20.15%; recovery is not assumed. All current claims must first be reconciled. The low-return exception does not rescue R here: reasonable current cash uncertainty crosses funded/unfunded, rather than simply changing an otherwise securely poor return. R is therefore NS, not an artificially discounted score.

Liquidity and position granularity: the official 19 October interoperability master verifies 600-share lot and 4,669,600 shares; its raw SM/ST rows do not mean an NSE listing. IIFL identifies current BSE group M. Its historical API yields 44 observed sessions out of 60 expected 24 July–19 October, with 16 unknown dates; 14 of 20 most recent sessions are observed. No missing date is asserted to be a zero-trade day. The 19 October record is one 600-share trade,₹46,860 actual published turnover. For observed 44 rows alone, mean turnover is ₹7.0373 lakh and median ₹3.7435 lakh; those are not the full 60-session statistics. Using missing turnover only as nonnegative unknowns, the full 60 mean is at least ₹5.1607 lakh (upper unbounded), median lies ₹2.0871–₹7.1571 lakh, and lower(mean,median) lies ₹2.0871–₹7.1571 lakh. These are mathematical missing-data bounds, not confidence intervals or invented zero fills. At 5% participation, the continuous ₹5 lakh exit estimate lies 13.97–47.91 sessions; at 2%, 34.93–119.78; at 10%, 6.99–23.96. Recent 20-session lower(mean,median) is bounded ₹0.97134–₹3.73476 lakh, suggesting even weaker current activity, not a reliable point estimate.

A ₹5 lakh position is not lot-exact: 10 lots cost ₹4,68,600,11 lots ₹5,15,460 at ₹78.10. The discrete test floors participation×actual/bounded volume÷600. At 5%, 32 observed sessions cannot accommodate one whole lot. Hence even if all 16 missing sessions had huge volume, the full 60-session median whole-lot capacity remains zero; 2% also has median zero,10% is bounded 0–1 lot. This does not prove an exit is impossible on every day, but no finite median-capacity exit estimate exists at 5%. Occasional larger prints cannot justify treating fractional lots as executable. Formal L remains NS because complete turnover/zero-day status and current ASM/GSM/ESM, spread, depth and circuit-lock evidence are missing. A historical July STASM entry is not current clearance. The dated master price-range field 62.48–93.72 is centered on 78.10 and is not asserted to be the 19 October intraday band. A direct 19 October BSE bhavcopy request returned 403 and was not retried. G4 is an implementation hold, not a fabricated suspension. Base roundtrip 1%/3%/5% buy and sell friction sensitivities reduce 19.47% to 19.00%/18.04%/17.10%, but they cannot substitute for absent depth or guarantee execution.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
A concentrated regional customer base delays payments just as railings/fixtures mix weakens; inventory bought for growth ties up cash; machinery requires advances before commissioning; extrusion margins are lower than expected; related-party leased-site improvements are difficult to recover. Public shareholders can suffer dilution or a permanent lower earnings multiple even if banks are repaid. The modest disclosed tax litigation is not the principal impairment mechanism.

The bear operating case is funded conditionally but ends ₹57.94,25.81% below entry over five years, with−5.80% annual return. A restrained survival case removes discretionary project deployment, leaves its ₹18.4 cr earmarked cash unavailable to creditors and excludes it from terminal equity, retains existing debt/current claims, funds 1% maintenance, uses−10% initial revenue/18% margin/60% core NWC and slow recovery. It remains cash-positive with minimum ₹4.20 cr under the synthetic opening. This test argues against declaring actual G3 failure from hypothetical aggressive expansion alone. It is not evidence unspent IPO cash can be diverted or that every project contract is cancelable.

A separate linked committed-project stress retains full quoted project cash plus ₹0.5 cr logistics/installation, initial revenue−20%, 12% margins,65% core NWC, and 10% loss on opening inventory+receivables (₹1.035 cr). The write-down reduces recoverable opening working capital once; it is not also charged as cash loss. It has a ₹0.331 cr early funding shortfall despite later positive cash, so no ordinary terminal price/IRR is reported. An additional unverified−₹2 cr stub-use sensitivity grows that gap to ₹2.331 cr. Those are conditional requirements, not a claim an actual payment was missed. An explicitly hypothetical equity rescue at 25% discount to the reference price supplies the exact cash gap, adds corresponding shares and yields about−16.31% diluted annual return; no rescue is assumed in the ordinary case. G3 remains uncertain pending dated balances and commitments, not failed based on this stress stack. Permanent-impairment risk: High, chiefly execution, collections, dilution and poor realizability of expansion assets, rather than proven insolvency.

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
At unchanged 4.6696 million shares,5×/10× prices are ₹390.50/₹781.00 and require equity values ₹182.35/₹364.71 cr. At a hypothetical 15× exit P/E and 15% net margin, sales would need about ₹81.05/₹162.09 cr: 4.60×/9.19× FY26, or roughly 35.7%/55.8% annual growth for five years. These equations ignore additional net cash/debt, and are clearly hurdle illustrations, not price forecasts. Further equity dilution increases required enterprise success per current share.

The bull model reaches approximately 5× price only by combining ₹65.28 cr sales,27% EBITDA margin, improving 44% core NWC,9× exit EBITDA and retained cash. It is not simply 8× nameplate times today's profit. High end-product throughput would require much larger distributor reach, product qualification, working capital and consistent collections. Railings/fixtures planned nameplate, different GFRP units and extrusion tonnes cannot be added into one fictitious capacity multiplier. Five-times is speculative but mechanically conceivable; ten-times is highly speculative and unsupported by verified demand or funding at the cutoff. Neither outcome is a compounder designation.

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
Before lifting the hold, obtain the signed FY26 accounts with all notes, current IPO bank/deployment statement and the March-to-October bridge: unrestricted versus earmarked cash, capital advances/invoices, fees already paid/accrued, OFS cost reimbursements, GST-credit eligibility/timing, debt maturities and all employee/statutory/tax/other claims. Resolve whether the ₹14.251209 cr quotation scope is still planned, contracted net/gross prices and freight/installation. No indicative bank proposal counts as funding.

Operating checkpoints: separate railings running feet, fixtures pieces and GFRPtonnes, realization/mix, own versus job-work margin, commissioned versus qualified machinery, and productive utilization. Reconcile customer totals and latest customer/supplier concentration. Demand evidence should be repeat collections and profitable shipment cohorts, not capacity or purchase-order headline alone. Cash checkpoints: latest debtor ageing, receipts after reporting date, inventory age/write-offs, related-party/security deposits and cash after maintenance. Sustained collections and normalized CFO/PAT moving toward 80% across several periods would materially improve CASH; one working-capital release would not establish a cycle record.

Governance checkpoints: related-party lease protection and rental/deposit changes, compensation normalization, trademark/design ownership, fire clearance, LEI status and tax-demand resolution, current pledges/ownership and auditor comments. Model falsification: margin below 20% without durable volume compensation, core working capital materially above 60% of revenue, unreconciled quote scope or an unfunded bank/contract claim. Implementation: verify lot 600, active group/surveillance/circuits, order-book depth and actual liquidity immediately before any contemplated order. This review does not place an order or choose a position size.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Research hold, pending evidence. Jivial has a real small manufacturing operation and potentially valuable extrusion integration, with profitable reported growth and historically modest bank debt. Its legacy returns deserve investigation, not dismissal. But persistent poor owner-cash realization, limited demonstrated moat, an acquisition-obscured growth series, customer/geographic concentration and a very large unseasoned project prevent calling it a quality compounder.

The conditional base model is useful for asking what must be true, not for issuing a buy target. A signed current cash/claims/deployment reconciliation can remove the IAS funding/model hold; a reliable underlying growth basis, through acquisition-adjusted history or sufficiently supported post-acquisition comparisons, is a separate requirement for REV and quality ranking. These are distinct from the liquidity hold and from a substantiated governance failure, which has not been established. Until resolved, do not rank a missing aggregate as zero or below scored businesses, and do not treat an illustrative ₹5 lakh exit calculation as portfolio suitability. The existing main-board reviews and public pages were not changed.

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
Primary signed 17 June prospectus and 30 June-signed/1 July published basis-of-allotment were recovered from legitimate independent public mirrors. Original financial annexures, cash-flow classification, machinery quote footnotes and the allotment advertisement were read; the latter was visually checked. FY26 directors and audit reports were read in complete independent HTML reproduction, not represented as the signed annual PDF. The auditor date is 22 July 2026; directors report date 4 September 2026. FY26 financial notes remain missing. Separate primary peer evidence and dated market cross-checks are retained.

Access restrictions were respected. The previously denied annual attachment eb 8481 cb-4 f 64-4 f 35-a 34 d-746 e 5 f 0 a 1 dd 3.pdf was not retried. BSE results 250740 ef-0431-4780-a 0 e 8-19 c 699 eeec 01.pdf, AGM0 fcdf 4 ca-4 d 47-40 d 4-90 d 1-4 f 7 f 85 aa 255 d.pdf and issuer home/investor pages returned 403 in this run and were not bypassed or retried. Independent mirrors were used only as separate public sources. No denied route is needed to reproduce the saved historical calculations.

Key unresolved questions are exact current cash/claims, IPO deployment and fee allocation, contracted machinery scope and GST cash timing, revenue acquired with the predecessor, latest collection/stock ageing, new-capacity commissioning and exact current trading restrictions. The full notes include forecast assumptions, source ledger, claim mapping, calculation code, annual case CSVs, sensitivity matrix and QA. Evidence gaps remain explicit. All material financial statements are in ₹crore unless shares/price/unit counts are stated; small one-lakh/one-thousand rounding differences are not escalated into misconduct. No future post-cutoff news or later price is used.

Market packet completed to available evidence: official lot/shares, dated secondary quote,44/60 actual-turnover rows, conservative missing-data bounds and lot-discrete capacity are saved. Sixteen dates and current surveillance remain unverified; the review is finalized with explicit gaps, not waiting for an unconfirmed source.

gates.reason: RPT/disclosure concerns but no substantiated severe minority harm; unmodified audit and favorable CARO retained.

Historical financial annexures remain usable. The post-deal growth comparison lacks complete volume/price–mix support; latest signed notes, dated current claims and IPO deployment are unavailable. Inconsistent promotional KPI tables are excluded.
The conditional essential-survival case is funded. A committed-project stress gap is not an actual default; dated cash and commitments are required.

Median whole-lot capacity is zero at 5% even with missing dates unbounded. Actual secondary turnover is available for 44 of 60 sessions; current restrictions and missing-day status are unverified. No suspension is asserted.

evidence.finding:
Jivial is a very small manufacturer of finished aluminium railings and fixtures, now attempting a much larger extrusion/backward-integration and GFRP expansion. It is not an aluminium smelter. Reported growth and legacy accounting returns are attractive, but neither establishes a durable competitive advantage or cash-generative new plant. FY26 revenue/PAT of ₹17.6343 cr/₹3.7540 cr are corroborated in a reproduced directors report; CFO was only about ₹0.5443 cr. Cumulative FY23–25 audited/restated CFO/PAT is 27.1%, falling to 13.4% after lease/security deposits. Inventory and receivables, rather than exceptional income, are the central economic concern.

At the dated 19 October ₹78.10 close, issued equity value is ₹36.4696 cr and static FY26 P/E is 9.72×. The 60% decline from the ₹196 IPO price is not a margin of safety by itself. A fully specified conditional annual base case produces 19.47% return, but that number is not eligible for R: actual October unrestricted cash, IPO deployment, exact opening claim composition and the January–October balance bridge are missing. The underlying growth basis also remains unresolved: the one full post-acquisition annual comparison lacks a complete volume/price–mix bridge and comparable interim history, so REV, BQS and GQS remain NS rather than fabricated point scores. This is a completed substantive deep review with targeted evidence holds, not a favorable investment recommendation. Classification: research hold / cash-conversion and execution watchlist; no compounder designation.

evidence.claim: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
evidence.finding:
Information cutoff 20 October 2026; price date 19 October 2026; nominal INR equity hurdle 15%; five annual periods ending 19 October 2027–2031; reference position ₹5 lakh, not a recommendation for the user's portfolio. Jivial Industries Limited, BSE SME544805/JIVIAL, ISIN INE0 V3 T01017, incorporated 23 June 2021 and converted to public company 1 January 2024. CIN U28999 GJ2021 PLC123516. Listing 1 July 2026; post-IPO shares 4,669,600. Accounts are standalone Indian GAAP/AS, no verified subsidiary/NCI complexity. A trading lot is 600 shares; the IPO minimum application was 1,200 shares, two lots.

G1 integrity: no substantiated severe failure established. Related-party property and predecessor acquisition warrant scrutiny, not allegations of diversion. G2 reliability: targeted hold on the current investment model and organic-growth comparability. Financial annexures are much more reliable than inconsistent promotional KPI tables; the latest signed annual notes and current cash/deployment bridge remain unavailable. This is not a finding that all historic accounts are false. G3 funding: uncertain, not failed. Low historical debt and received IPO proceeds support the business, but earmarks and an unresolved machinery quote/GST allocation matter. Restrained essential operations survive in the disclosed conditional test; a linked committed-project stress has a cash gap. A modeled stress gap is not evidence of an actual default. G4 tradability: implementation hold: 44/60 turnover rows recovered and median 5% whole-lot capacity is demonstrably zero; exact missing-day status/current restrictions remain unavailable.

High confidence: identity, original prospectus financial facts and IPO terms. Medium: FY26 reproduced P&L/audit, approximate balance sheet, historical qualitative judgments. Low: exact October cash/claims, commissioned capacity and organic acquisition-adjusted growth. Missing evidence is not scored neutral 5.

Canonical factors: GOV 5, MOAT 4, REV NS, DUR 5, CAP 5, CASH 2, BAL 5, EXEC 5, EARN 5, R NS, D4, P5; L remains NS after the bounded liquidity review. Each factor has a separate evidence/contrary-evidence audit. GOV 5 is mixed stewardship, not a governance clearance. CASH 2 reflects persistent realized weakness, not merely a first-year growth investment. CAP 5 does not ignore high legacy returns; it recognizes that they do not prove returns on the much larger funded project. BAL 5 assesses the identifiable low-debt structure, while G3 remains an uncertainty about dated funding, not an arbitrary failure.

BQS known contribution 3.90, coverage 88%, missing-data mathematical bound 4.02–5.10 before one-decimal display, not a confidence interval. GQS known contribution 2.70, coverage 60%, mathematical bound 3.10–6.70; the persistent CASH≤3 cap would limit any scoreable final GQS to 5.0. Do not replace NS with the cap. IAS is NS because Q/BQS, R and initially L are incomplete; no renormalization or midpoint. Scores and bounds are analyst judgments, not verified facts. BQS/GQS ranking eligibility is withheld for the specific underlying REV evidence gap, despite one comparable post-acquisition annual growth observation; IAS has separate current-funding/model and implementation gaps. Resolving liquidity alone will not make any investment ranking eligible. CAP and GOV ±1 sensitivity moves BQS known contribution±0.12 and±0.20 respectively; CAP and EARN ±1 each move GQS±0.15. A0.1-point comparison would be false precision.

Jivial buys unfinished aluminium extrusions/castings, then cuts, drills, anodizes, buffs/polishes and powder-coats them. Products include bottom glass-holding profiles, handrails, spigots, bends, brackets, jointers, locks and endcaps. Revenue depends on design/specification, finish, availability, channel service and material prices, not only tonnes of aluminium. Buyers include fabricators, glass suppliers, construction SMEs, architects and interior designers. Orders are purchase-order based, without long-term customer or supplier commitments. The prospectus reports 35 distributors and customer count increasing 291→327; those relationships are useful distribution, not contractual recurring revenue.

FY25 railings ₹9.3883 cr contributed 78.2%, fixtures ₹2.0122 cr 16.76%, other ₹0.6055 cr 5.04%. In 9 MDecember 25 railings reached ₹9.8849 cr 81.6%, fixtures ₹0.573 cr 4.73%, other ₹1.6557 cr 13.67%. This large mix shift must be understood before extrapolating margins. Gujarat/Maharashtra/Chhattisgarh represented 72.86% of FY25 sales and 78.97% of 9 MDecember 25 sales. The business is regionally concentrated rather than an already national franchise.

Unit I is about 6,500 sqft and leased; the larger Unit II is about 40,000 sqft, also leased. There were 19 permanent staff at 31 May 2026 and 15–18 daily workers. The first plant's small asset base, outsourced job work and related-party lease economics partly explain high legacy capital returns. The proposed extrusion presses change power, tooling, maintenance, process-control and working-capital requirements. GFRP is a new adjacent capability, not proven demand automatically created by capex.

MOAT 4: finish, design assortment and local distributor service are real but contestable advantages. No independently verified market share, customer retention cohort, price premium or exclusive specification was found. Suppliers and customers are not locked in by long-term contracts. The company describes three patents, but the detailed evidence includes registered industrial designs, not verified broad utility-patent protection; the trademark was promoter-owned and assigned 5 July 2024. Do not turn that wording into a proprietary-technology moat.

Top-ten suppliers supplied about 87% of FY25 purchases, and the largest about 40.7%. Customer concentration is rising, but the exact latest figure is internally inconsistent: the risk section reports ₹7.7215 cr/63.74%; detailed customer amounts total ₹7.2215 cr, which divided by ₹12.1135 cr is 59.62%, versus a printed 59.04%. The largest listed customer is about 22.2%. These are not three independent confirmations. The defensible conclusion is material concentration plus a disclosure reconciliation gap, not the most favorable percentage.

Peer economics show why a mechanical aluminium-sector P/E is inappropriate. ANB Metal Cast is an extrusion manufacturer: official FY26 standalone revenue ₹225.1908 cr, PAT ₹21.4596 cr, derived ex-other-income EBITDA ₹32.4507 cr/14.4%, and CFO−₹38.3258 cr. Its weak cash flow is a sector funding warning, not an excuse for Jivial. Euro Panel's issuer FY26 consolidated headline is about ₹503.20 cr revenue/₹26.56 cr PAT, roughly 5.3% net margin, but aluminium composite façade panels have different inputs/channel/brand economics. Sudal is a more established extrusion comparator for the proposed backward integration, not a like-for-like finished-railings valuation. Jivial's FY26 derived 27.5% EBITDA margin is much higher, making mix, normalization and competitive durability essential questions. Peer multiples were not independently established at the cutoff, so no spurious target multiple average is used.

Audited/restated FY23/FY24/FY25 revenue was ₹8.3993/₹11.0573/₹12.0061 cr. FY26 independently reproduced revenue is ₹17.6343 cr. Annual additions were ₹2.6580 cr,₹0.9488 cr and ₹5.6282 cr; growth 31.65%, 8.58% and 46.88% by exact table amounts (management rounds 46.98%, which does not exactly match those amounts). FY23–25 CAGR is 19.56% across two intervals, not the prospectus KPI's 12.65% calculation. Reported FY23–26 three-year CAGR is 28.05%. Five/ten-year CAGRs are unavailable: incorporation was 2021 and FY22 is a short initial period, not a six-observation five-year record.

The September 2023 acquisition of promoter Anand's predecessor business for ₹0.51 cr created ₹0.4246 cr goodwill. Acquired sales/profits and like-for-like organic revenue are not separately disclosed. Production grew: railings 100,800→140,890→156,330 running feet in FY23–25, fixtures 110,400→152,460→169,400 pieces. These corroborate activity growth but do not isolate acquisition, mix or selling prices. FY25 and FY26 are genuinely comparable full post-acquisition years, with 46.88% reported growth, so the older transaction alone is not a reason to withhold REV. Nevertheless, this supplies only one annual comparison; complete FY26 railings/fixtures/GFRP volumes, realization and a price–mix bridge are missing, while disclosed product mix changed sharply. Comparable prior interim data are also unavailable. Those gaps prevent a reliable underlying multi-year growth basis, rather than merely a long history, so REV remains NS after reassessment. A conservative score is not invented simply to complete the aggregate.

The 9 MDecember 25 figures are ₹12.1135 cr revenue and ₹2.9477 cr restated PAT. They are not annualized into a forecast, and their cash flow is not compared with a full year as a growth rate. FY26 minus 9 M gives an indicative ₹5.5208 cr final-quarter revenue, but no prior comparable 9 M/quarter series supports a trustworthy TTM or interim trajectory adjustment. As of the cutoff, FY26 is the latest complete year recovered, not a claim that all FY27 trading is known.

Legacy annual capacity is 193,000 running feet of railings and 242,000 fixtures; FY25 production implies 81%/70% utilization. Nine-month output 128,828 feet/141,570 fixtures equals 66.75%/58.5% of annual capacity, not evidence of a full-year utilization collapse. Planned capacity 1.58 million feet/1.985 million fixtures is about 8.2× current nameplate. GFRP capacity 420 MT with 61.74 MT9 M production is far from mature utilization; proposed capacity is 1,248 MT. Capacity is an upper production constraint, not a forecast of orders or sales.

Fresh IPO proceeds ₹26.64816 cr less stated ₹4.2543 cr expenses produce ₹22.39386 cr net: ₹14.4 cr machinery,₹4.0 cr renovation and ₹3.99386 cr general corporate purposes. The ₹5.33904 cr OFS belongs to selling promoters, not the company. Substantial lead-manager/underwriting/selling expenses are disclosed, but fee size alone does not prove misconduct. The signed allotment advertisement shows 103,200 shares devolved on underwriters,6.32% of the offered issue, after an individual-category shortfall; this tempers claims of enthusiastic validated demand.

The machinery table totals ₹14.251209 cr excluding GST, while the ₹14.4 cr allocation includes 18% GST. An unchanged quoted scope would need ₹16.81643 cr machinery cash, plus ₹4.006303 cr renovation: ₹20.82273 cr versus ₹18.4 cr earmarked, a ₹2.42273 cr gross-cash difference before extra freight/installation. The issuer explicitly permits revising machinery/model/quantity, and says shortfalls may use internal accruals, GCP or debt. No definitive machine orders existed at 17 June; quotations dated 8–9 June generally last 180 days/six months, electrical quote five months. All quoted equipment may not ultimately be bought unchanged. This is an unresolved scope/timing budget inconsistency, not proof of a certain overrun or default.

The model separates gross GST cash from possible input-tax-credit realization. Base assumes no cash recovery and depreciates a net-of-GST illustrative basis, not double-expensing GST. Conditional half/full machinery-GST recovery in year 2 is shown separately; eligibility, output-tax offset and timing are unverified, and no instant refund is assumed. Capex needs order/advance, delivery, installation, qualification and commercial-ramp evidence. September management says no deviation from objects, but no signed deployment reconciliation was recovered. Promises-versus-delivery: current capacity/production is verified through December; IPO completed June/July; machine procurement, commissioning and productive sales remain ND at 20 October. The base ends ₹42.74 cr sales,2.42× FY26, below nameplate's 8× expansion but still requires customers and working-capital discipline, not merely capacity.

Promoters are Anand Jitendrabhai Chovatiya and Sheetalben Anand Chovatiya; management biographies claim roughly 9/6 years relevant experience. Unclassified ₹2.44 cr other assets are not added to free cash or terminal recovery, so no assumed tax refund, deposit release or NFO realization offsets claims. Prior prepaid expenses could overlap: ₹0.4382 cr existed at December 25, but March/October exact fee prepayment/payable composition and OFS cost reimbursement are unknown. Net GST is not expensed twice; possible recovery is separate. Annual cash being positive does not prove within-year liquidity or purchase-order payment timing. A separate linked committed-project stress retains full quoted project cash plus ₹0.5 cr logistics/installation, initial revenue−20%, 12% margins,65% core NWC, and 10% loss on opening inventory+receivables (₹1.035 cr). At unchanged 4.6696 million shares,5×/10× prices are ₹390.50/₹781.00 and require equity values ₹182.35/₹364.71 cr. The bull model reaches approximately 5× price only by combining ₹65.28 cr sales,27% EBITDA margin, improving 44% core NWC,9× exit EBITDA and retained cash. Before lifting the hold, obtain the signed FY26 accounts with all notes, current IPO bank/deployment statement and the March-to-October bridge: unrestricted versus earmarked cash, capital advances/invoices, fees already paid/accrued, OFS cost reimbursements, GST-credit eligibility/timing, debt maturities and all employee/statutory/tax/other claims. Operating checkpoints: separate railings running feet, fixtures pieces and GFRPtonnes, realization/mix, own versus job-work margin, commissioned versus qualified machinery, and productive utilization. Implementation: verify lot 600, active group/surveillance/circuits, order-book depth and actual liquidity immediately before any contemplated order. This review does not place an order or choose a position size.

Research hold, pending evidence. Jivial has a real small manufacturing operation and potentially valuable extrusion integration, with profitable reported growth and historically modest bank debt. Its legacy returns deserve investigation, not dismissal. But persistent poor owner-cash realization, limited demonstrated moat, an acquisition-obscured growth series, customer/geographic concentration and a very large unseasoned project prevent calling it a quality compounder.

The conditional base model is useful for asking what must be true, not for issuing a buy target. A signed current cash/claims/deployment reconciliation can remove the IAS funding/model hold; a reliable underlying growth basis, through acquisition-adjusted history or sufficiently supported post-acquisition comparisons, is a separate requirement for REV and quality ranking. These are distinct from the liquidity hold and from a substantiated governance failure, which has not been established. Until resolved, do not rank a missing aggregate as zero or below scored businesses, and do not treat an illustrative ₹5 lakh exit calculation as portfolio suitability.
